raw_response:
Answer: A
Reason: The chest X-rays demonstrate a massive right-sided pneumothorax with significant mediastinal shift to the right and an abnormal, distorted cardiac silhouette in the right hemithorax. These findings are characteristic of right-sided cardiac herniation through a pericardial defect (often following pneumonectomy), where the heart prolapses into the empty pleural space, causing acute haemodynamic compromise due to torsion and obstruction of the great vessels.
